{{Nihongo|'''Rui Hachimura'''|八村 塁|Hachimura Rui|{{ipa|ja|hatɕiꜜmɯɾa ɾɯꜜi|lang}}, born February 8, 1998|lead=yes}} is a Japanese professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga Bulldogs]] and has played for the [[Japan national basketball team|Japan national team]]. He plays the [[power forward]] position.<ref name=br/> After being selected ninth overall by the [[Washington Wizards]] in the [[2019 NBA draft]], he was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie Second Team]] in 2020.

Born in [[Toyama Prefecture]], Hachimura achieved success at the youth level in Japan, leading [[Sendai University Meisei High School|Meisei High School]] to three straight All-Japan High School Tournament titles and being a top player for the Japanese [[Japan national under-17 basketball team|under-17]] and [[Japan national under-19 basketball team|under-19]] national teams in [[FIBA]] competition. He joined Gonzaga in 2016 as the fifth Japanese-born men's [[NCAA Division I]] player and in 2017 became the first Japanese national to play in the [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA Division I men's tournament]]. As a sophomore, he earned first-team All-WCC honors. He was named a finalist for the [[Naismith College Player of the Year|Naismith Player of the Year]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Woodburn |first1=Peter |title=Rui Hachimura named Naismith Player of the Year finalist |url=https://www.slipperstillfits.com/2019/3/19/18272778/naismith-player-of-the-year-finalist-rui-hachimura |website=The Slipper Still Fits |date=March 19, 2019 |publisher=SB Nation |access-date= March 22, 2019}}</ref>

==Early life and career==
[[File:Hachimura rui (cropped).jpg|right|thumb|Hachimura with [[Sendai University Meisei High School|Meisei High School]] in 2016]]

Hachimura was born on February 8, 1998, in [[Toyama Prefecture]], Japan, to a Japanese mother, {{nihongo|Makiko|麻紀子}} and a [[Benin]]ese father, Zakari Jabil. His given name, {{Nihongo||塁|Rui}}, means "base" or "fortress" in Japanese; the name was given to him by his grandfather because he was a big fan of [[baseball]] (the character 塁 is also used for "[[Baseball field|base]]" in context of baseball). His surname is from his mother's [[koseki|family register]]. He has three younger siblings—one brother and two sisters. Hachimura's younger brother, {{ill|Allen Hachimura|ja|八村阿蓮|lt=Allen}}, played basketball at [[Tokai University]] and is also a professional basketball player for the [[Kobe Storks]] of the [[B.League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Rui Hachimura's profile |url= https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/110364/sid/13204/tid/309/tid2//_/2017_FIBA_U19_Basketball_World_Cup/index.html |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20181112021430/https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/110364/sid/13204/tid/309/tid2//_/2017_FIBA_U19_Basketball_World_Cup/index.html |url-status= dead |archive-date= November 12, 2018 |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=November 10, 2018}}</ref><ref name= "mandel">{{cite web |last1=Mandel |first1=Stewart |title=Japan will be watching the Final Four just to see this guy you probably don't know |url= https://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/gonzaga-rui-hachimura-ncaa-tournament-final-four-japan-033017 |work=[[Fox Sports (United States)|Fox Sports]] |access-date=November 10, 2018 |date=March 30, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title=選手 | website=神戸ストークス | url=https://www.storks.jp/team/players/ | language=ja | access-date=May 15, 2026}}</ref> In his childhood, he played [[baseball]] as a [[catcher]] and [[pitcher]].<ref name= "wintercup">{{cite web |last1=Nagatsuka |first1=Kaz |title=Hachimura powers Meisei High to Winter Cup title |url= https://www.japantimes.co.jp/sports/2013/12/29/basketball/hachimura-powers-meisei-high-to-winter-cup-title/#.W-b095NKjIU |website=[[The Japan Times]] |access-date=November 10, 2018 |date=December 29, 2013}}</ref> On December 29, 2013, Hachimura led the [[Sendai University Meisei High School|Meisei High School]] basketball team to its second title in the All-Japan High School Tournament, scoring 32 points in a 92–78 win over Fukuoka University Ohori. In 2014, he helped his team win the tournament for a second straight year.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Nagatsuka |first1= Kaz |title=Hachimura guides Meisei High to impressive victory in Winter Cup opener |url=https://www.japantimes.co.jp/sports/2015/12/25/basketball/hachimura-guides-meisei-high-to-impressive-victory-in-winter-cup-opener/#.W-b4iJNKjIU |website=[[The Japan Times]] |access-date=November 10, 2018 |date=December 25, 2015}}</ref> In April 2015, Hachimura was invited to the [[Jordan Brand Classic]], where he recorded nine points and five rebounds in the International Game.<ref name="future">{{cite web |last1=Nagatsuka |first1=Kaz |title=Future looking bright for Japanese men's basketball |url= https://www.japantimes.co.jp/sports/2015/06/22/basketball/future-looking-bright-japanese-mens-basketball/#.W-b2lJNKjIU |website=[[The Japan Times]] |access-date=November 10, 2018 |date=June 22, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url = http://jordanbrandclassic.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/Box-Score-International-Game.pdf|title = Jordan Brand Classic Box Score International Game|date = April 17, 2015 |access-date = November 10, 2018 |publisher = [[Jordan Brand Classic]]}}</ref>

On November 21, 2015, he signed a [[National Letter of Intent]] to play [[college basketball]] for the [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga Bulldogs]] in the US, being considered by [[ESPN]] as one of the best international players entering college.<ref>{{Cite web |url= https://insider.espn.com/blog/ncbrecruiting/on-the-trail/insider/post?id=12808 |title=The next wave of international prospects |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |date=January 31, 2015 |website= ESPN.com |access-date=December 6, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=MBB Signs Hachimura to National Letter of Intent |url= https://gozags.com/news/2015/11/21/MBB_Signs_Hachimura_to_National_Letter_of_Intent.aspx |publisher=Gonzaga University Athletics |access-date= November 10, 2018 |date=November 21, 2015}}</ref> On December 29, 2015, Hachimura posted 34 points, 19 rebounds and three blocks to guide Meisei past Tsuchiura Nihon University High School for his third All-Japan Tournament victory.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Nagatsuka |first1= Kaz |title=Hachimura lifts Meisei High to Winter Cup three-peat |url= https://www.japantimes.co.jp/sports/2015/12/29/basketball/hachimura-lifts-meisei-high-winter-cup-three-peat/#.W-b2HZNKjIU |website=[[The Japan Times]] |access-date=November 10, 2018 |date=December 29, 2015}}</ref>

Despite signing with Gonzaga in the early signing period for 2016, Hachimura's eligibility to play college basketball was called into question.<ref>{{Cite web |url= http://www.spokesman.com/stories/2015/nov/20/zags-sign-japanese-forward-rui-hachimura/ |title=Zags sign Japanese forward Rui Hachimura |last=Meehan |first=Jim |date=November 20, 2015 |website=The Spokesman-Review |access-date=December 6, 2019}}</ref> The concerns were that he needed to acclimate better culturally and linguistically to the US and would potentially need to attend a [[College-preparatory school|prep school]] before entering Gonzaga or [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirting]] if eligible.<ref name= "Tommy Lloyd">{{Cite web |url= http://www.heinnews.com/basketball/nba/next-international-wave-will-set-up-zags-for-a-while-says-gus-lloyd/ |title=Next international wave will set up Zags for a while, says GU's Lloyd |date=December 9, 2015 |website= heinnews.com |access-date=December 6, 2019}}</ref> In February 2016, Hachimura claimed to understand 80 percent of English but speak only 30–40 percent of it.<ref>{{cite web|title=Talking afterwards to Rui Hachimura (1998 Japan) he says he understands 80% of English, can only talk about 30-40% though. Finals in March|url=https://twitter.com/heinnews/status/698588173815959556|date=February 13, 2016}}</ref> By April 2016, Hachimura was still studying for the [[SAT]] to gain entrance to college.<ref>{{Cite web |url= http://sports.yahoo.co.jp/column/detail/201604080006-spnavi |title=Rui Hachimura talks about high school graduation and future goals in the United States, A New Journey |last=Konaga |first=Yoshinaga |date=April 11, 2016 |website=Yahoo! Sports |language=en-JP |access-date=December 6, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite tweet |title=Questions still for Rui Hachimura if he'll pass tests to get into Gonzaga. Hopefully he's hitting books hard instead of coming to #AST2016| user= heinnews | number= 714424351085473793| date=March 28, 2016}}</ref> In May 2016, Hachimura announced that he met the SAT and GPA requirements to be eligible to play at Gonzaga beginning as early as fall 2016. He planned to play as a true freshman and did not [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] his first year.<ref>{{Cite web |url= http://www.japantimes.co.jp/sports/2016/05/11/basketball/hachimura-cleared-to-enroll-at-gonzaga/#.VzNEH4QrLIW |title=Hachimura cleared to enroll at Gonzaga |last=Nagatsuka |first=Kaz |date=May 11, 2016 |website=The Japan Times |access-date=December 6, 2019}}</ref>{{College athlete recruit start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2016}}

==Professional career==

===Washington Wizards (2019–2023)===
[[File:Rui Hachimura Yuta Watanabe (50640688868).jpg|thumb|In 2020 with [[Yuta Watanabe]] of the [[Toronto Raptors]]]]
On April 15, 2019, Hachimura announced that he would forgo his final year of eligibility and declared for the [[2019 NBA draft]],<ref>{{Cite magazine| title=Gonzaga's Rui Hachimura Declares for NBA Draft| last=Jones | first= Kaelen| url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2019/04/15/rui-hachimura-gonzaga-declares-nba-draft|date=April 15, 2019|access-date=May 9, 2019| magazine=Sports Illustrated}}</ref> where he was drafted ninth overall by the [[Washington Wizards]]. Hachimura was the second Japanese-born player to be drafted into the NBA after [[Yasutaka Okayama]], who was drafted 171st overall in the [[1981 NBA draft]], and also the first Japanese player ever taken in the first round.<ref>{{Cite magazine|title=2019 NBA draft: Rui Hachimura is first Japanese-born player drafted | via= SI.com| last=Caron | first= Emily|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2019/06/20/gonzaga-rui-hachimura-first-japanese-born-player-drafted|date=June 20, 2019|magazine=Sports Illustrated|access-date=June 20, 2019}}</ref> On October 23, 2019, Hachimura made his NBA debut, posting a double-double (14 points, 10 rebounds) as a starter in a 100–108 loss to the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401160631 |title=Doncic-Porzingis debut carries Mavs past Wizards, 108-100 |date=October 23, 2019 |website=ESPN.com |access-date= October 23, 2019 |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> On December 1, 2019, Hachimura scored a then career-high 30 points in a 125–150 loss to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] along with nine rebounds, three assists and a steal.<ref>{{cite web| url= https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401160934|title=Clippers blow out undermanned Wizards 150-125| date= December 1, 2019| agency= Associated Press| website= ESPN.com| access-date=December 1, 2019}}</ref>

In December 2019, he and [[Yuta Watanabe]] of the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] became the first pair of Japanese players to face each other in the NBA.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Buckner |first1=Candace |title=For Wizards' Rui Hachimura, Memphis trip brings a pair of special reunions |url= https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2019/12/15/wizards-rui-hachimura-memphis-trip-brings-pair-special-reunions/ |access-date=January 6, 2020 |newspaper=[[Washington Post]] |date= December 15, 2019}}</ref>{{Failed verification|date=February 2021}} Hachimura suffered a groin injury against the [[Detroit Pistons]] on December 16 and had surgery and missed several games.<ref>{{cite news |title=Wizards' Rui Hachimura (groin) to be reevaluated in two weeks |url= https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/28423519/wizards-rui-hachimura-groin-reevaluated-two-weeks |access-date=January 5, 2020 |work= ESPN.com |agency= Associated Press |date=January 5, 2020}}</ref>

On September 15, 2020, Hachimura was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie Second Team]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Ja Morant, Zion Williamsom headline 2019-20 Kia All-Rookie First Team |url= https://www.nba.com/article/2020/09/15/nba-2019-20-all-rookie-first-team-official-release |website=NBA.com |access-date= September 15, 2020}}</ref>

On March 30, 2021, Hachimura tied his then career high of 30 points in a 104–114 loss to the [[Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=ROZIER SCORES 27 POINTS, LEADS HORNETS PAST WIZARDS 114-104 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000718 |access-date=February 1, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On May 23, he made his playoff debut during the first round, recording 12 points and five rebounds in a 118–125 Game 1 loss to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=HARRIS SCORES 37, LEADS 76ERS PAST WIZARDS 125-118 IN GAME 1 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042000101 |access-date=February 1, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On May 31, Hachimura logged 20 points and a career-high 13 rebounds in a 122–114 Game 4 win.<ref>{{Cite web |title=EMBIID LEAVES WITH SORE KNEE, 76ERS LOSE TO WIZARDS 122-114 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042000104 |access-date=February 1, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> The Wizards ended up losing the series in five games.

On September 25, 2021, the Wizards announced that Hachimura had been excused from the start of training camp for personal reasons.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wizards forward Rui Hachimura to miss start of training camp |url=https://www.nba.com/news/wizards-forward-rui-hachimura-to-miss-start-of-training-camp |access-date=February 1, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> He made his season debut on January 9, 2022, recording six points and three rebounds in a 102–100 win over the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=KUZMA'S 22 BOARDS LIFT WIZARDS OVER MAGIC 102-100 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100598 |access-date=February 1, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> During the 2021–22 NBA season, Hachimura played 42 games while averaging 11.3 points per game, 3.8 rebounds per game, and 1.1 assists per game.<ref name=br>{{Cite web |title=Rui Hachimura Stats |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/hachiru01.html |access-date=2022-05-01 |website=Basketball-Reference.com}}</ref> This represented a slight dip in his career averages. However, his three-point shooting improved dramatically: Hachimura's 44.7 percent rate was second only to Luke Kennard (44.9 percent) among NBA players with at least 100 attempts.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.nbcsports.com/washington/wizards/how-sustainable-rui-hachimuras-improvement-3-point-shooter | title=How sustainable is Hachimura's 3-point shooting?}}</ref>

On January 21, 2023, in his last game before being traded, Hachimura recorded a then career-high-tying 30 points, alongside five rebounds and two blocks, in a 138–118 win over the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=HACHIMURA SCORES 30 TO LEAD WIZARDS OVER MAGIC 138-118 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200693 |access-date=February 1, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Lakers (2023–2026)===

On January 23, 2023, Hachimura was traded to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in exchange for [[Kendrick Nunn]] and three second-round draft picks.<ref>{{cite web |title=Los Angeles Lakers Acquire Rui Hachimura |url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/los-angeles-lakers-acquire-rui-hachimura-1-23-23 |access-date=January 23, 2023 |work=NBA.com |date=January 23, 2023}}</ref> Hachimura made his Lakers debut two days later, recording 12 points and six rebounds in a 113–104 win over the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Davis scores 21 points in return as Lakers defeat Spurs |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401468884 |access-date=January 26, 2023 |website=ESPN}}</ref>

In the [[2023 NBA playoffs]], Hachimura was a vital part of the Lakers rotation on both ends of the court. He scored 29 points in his Lakers post-season debut to lead the team to a first-round Game 1 victory over the No. 2-seeded [[Memphis Grizzlies]], and in the Western Conference Finals, was frequently given the defensive assignment of guarding Denver's offensive juggernaut [[Nikola Jokić]], allowing LA's defensive linchpin [[Anthony Davis]] more freedom to roam the court as a help defender. Los Angeles would end up losing the series to Denver in 4 games. For the 2022-2023 season, Hachimura averaged 11.2 points, 4.5 rebounds, and  shot 48.6% on field goals.<ref name="career">{{cite web |title=Rui Hachimura Career Stats |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/stats/_/id/4066648/rui-hachimura |website=ESPN |access-date=1 November 2025}}</ref>

On July 6, 2023, Hachimura re-signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Los Angeles Lakers Re-Sign Rui Hachimura |url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/los-angeles-lakers-re-sign-rui-hachimura-070623 |access-date=July 6, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On December 9, 2023, Hachimura and the Lakers won the [[2023 NBA In-Season Tournament|inaugural season]] of the [[NBA In-Season Tournament]] (also known as the NBA Cup).<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Bontemps |first=Tim |date=2023-12-10 |title=Lakers take NBA Cup as AD explodes for 41-20 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/39080368/lakers-win-nba-cup-lebron-james-earns-season-tournament-mvp |access-date=2023-12-10 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

On February 14, 2024, Hachimura set a new career high of 36 points in a 138–122 victory over the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rui's Career Night Propels Lakers Past Jazz|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/ruis-career-night-propels-lakers-past-jazz |access-date=February 14, 2024 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On March 27, Hachimura put up 32 points on a career-high seven made three-pointers and 10 rebounds in a 136–124 win over the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/lakers-rui-hachimura-memphiz-grizzlies-los-angeles-lebron-james|title=Rui Hachimura continues ownership of Memphis in Lakers win vs. Grizzlies|website=ClutchPoints|last=Corvo|first=Michael|date=March 27, 2024|access-date=March 27, 2024}}</ref>  For the season, he raised his scoring average to 13.6 ppg while shooting a career high 53.7% on two-point shots and increasing his three-point-percentage 11 points, to 42%.<ref name= career/>

In 2024–25, Hachimura's scoring average remained steady at 13.1 ppg while his two-point percentage was 50.1% and his three-point percentage was 41.3.  The most points he scored in a game during the season was 24, doing so in a 124–117 win over the [[Indiana Pacers]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Austin Reaves scores a career-high 45, and the Lakers shock the Pacers 124–117 without Luka, LeBron |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/game/_/gameId/401705308/pacers-lakers |website=ESPN |access-date=November 1, 2025}}</ref> and in a 123–116 loss to the [[Golden State Warriors]] on April 3.<ref>{{cite news |title=Curry scores 37 and Warriors win 123–116 in a potential first round playoff series |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/game/_/gameId/401705308/pacers-lakers |access-date=November 1, 2025 |publisher=ESPN |date=April 3, 2025}}</ref> In a first-round playoff loss to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], he scored 14.8 points-per-game while shooting 49.1% on two-pointers and 48.4% on three-pointers.<ref name=career />

On December 4, 2025, Hachimura made the first game-winning buzzer-beater of his career.  Along the way, he scored 12 points while hitting the three-pointer as time ran out to give the Lakers a 123–120 win over the [[Toronto Raptors]]<ref>{{cite news|first=Thuc Nhi|last=Nguyen|title=LeBron James’ record scoring streak ends, but Austin Reaves and Rui Hachimura deliver win|date=December 4, 2025|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/lakers/story/2025-12-04/los-angeles-lakers-toronto-raptors-nba-game-recap|access-date=December 4, 2025}}</ref>

During the 2025-2026 [[NBA playoffs]], Hachimura had shot the highest 3 point percentage in NBA playoff history. Shooting 51.8% from the 3 point line.

=== Los Angeles Clippers (2026–present) === 
On July 6, 2026, Hachimura officially signed with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] to a two-year, $28 million deal.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rui Hachimura, Clippers agree to two-year deal |url=https://www.nba.com/news/rui-hachimura-free-agency-2026 |access-date=2026-07-07 |website=NBA.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=CLIPPERS SIGN HACHIMURA {{!}} LA Clippers |url=https://clippers.com/news/clippers-sign-hachimura |access-date=2026-07-07 |website=clippers.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Senior national team===
[[File:20180917 FIBA Basketball World Cup Qualifier Japan vs Iran (44019576184).jpg|right|thumb|Hachimura after a 2019 FIBA World Cup qualification game with Japan]]

In a qualification round for the [[2019 FIBA World Cup]], Hachimura scored 25 points to help Japan defeat Iran 70–56.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Dauster |first1=Rob |title=Rui Hachimura scores 25 as Japan upsets Iran in World Cup qualifier |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2018/09/18/rui-hachimura-scores-25-as-japan-upsets-iran-in-world-cup-qualifier/ |access-date=September 21, 2018 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=September 18, 2018}}</ref>

Hachimura scored a game high 34 points in a loss to [[Slovenia men's national basketball team|Slovenia]] during the preliminary round of the [[2020 Summer Olympics|2020 Olympics]] in Tokyo.

Hachimura was called up for the [[2023 FIBA World Cup]], but ultimately withdrew on 27 June citing exhaustion from the NBA season and playoffs, in which his team had made the Western Conference Finals, and also citing the need to prepare for the following NBA season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kano |first=Shintaro |date=27 June 2023 |title=Japan's Rui Hachimura passes on FIBA Basketball World Cup 2023 |url=https://olympics.com/en/news/fiba-basketball-world-cup-rui-hachimura |access-date=28 August 2023 |website=Olympic Games}}</ref>
